facts: Bookworm libzstd 1.5.4+dfsg2-5 remains vulnerable; no Bookworm fixed version is listed.
Trixie security contains fixed version 1.5.7+dfsg-1+deb13u1; this is a different distribution branch and is not an authorized patch for these images.
The tracker links upstream fix commit 0c9d297531a9f15a717ff24604afc0843b3b1427 (v1.6.0).
A crafted compressed stream may disclose uninitialized or prior-context memory via decompressed output; default internal buffer size is 64 KiB.
An attacker needs to submit compressed input and observe the resulting output.
Version 1.6.0 fixes this CVE; the release notes identify a streaming-decompression disclosure with malformed input.
The fix bounds expired external history after a streaming output wrap and initializes decoder-owned literal padding.
pg_dump supports zstd compression for appropriate dump/archive formats.
pg_restore restores non-plain-text pg_dump archives. Untrusted dumps also present independent SQL execution risks.
When compiled with zstd support and configured for zstd WAL compression, PostgreSQL decompresses page images during WAL replay.
wal_compression defaults to off; its effective value on the retained image/runtime has not been checked by this review.

decision.r23: Independent; no closure or speculative upgrade implied.
decision.gate: Fresh explicit R20 review is required for the now-42-CVE conservative residual inventory and four exact image IDs. This report is evidence, not risk acceptance or formal MVP closure.
